title: A Land of Mosques and Marabouts
short_title: A Land of Mosques and Marabouts

history.note: Title page typed line by line as printed.

summary: The Hon. Mrs. Greville-Nugent (Ermengarda Greville-Nugent, née Ogilvy) spent some months of 1892–93 with her husband in Algiers, with excursions inland, and then went by sea to Tunis. She describes the Arab and Jewish quarters of Algiers, its cafés, shops, and mosques; Arab families at home, a wedding feast, conjurers, the scorpion-eating Aïssouas, and dancers; lessons in Arabic; the legends of the city’s mosques and marabouts; the country round Algiers, a Kabyle village, and the orange groves and gorges of Blidah. In Tunisia she visits Bizerta and a boys’ school, the bazaars of Tunis, a Jewish wedding, the city by night in Ramadan, the Bardo and the palace of Kassar-Saïd, and the ruins of Carthage. Short appendices treat the Ouled-Naïl dancers, spoken and literary Arabic, and a French writer’s account of a visit of French ministers to Algiers.
omitted_from_reading: The half-titles, printed contents, and list of illustrations are in the JSON only.
notes_on_text: The author is identified in library catalogues as Ermengarda Greville-Nugent; the dates of her life are from Burke’s Peerage (died 1949).
A few words of Arabic printed in the dedication and in Appendix B are given in Arabic script. The year in the dedication is printed with its digits reversed (٣٩٨١ for ١٨٩٣); it is corrected.
